# Comms declaration fixture

This source overlay extends the accepted home/runtime fixture on the invented five-seat Harbor/Orchard workplace. It adds the selected Comms body, one relative mail path and thirteen reach statements. It preserves the base Structure, Access, Agents, Homes and Runtime source and selects no Identity layer.

```sh
bash tests/fixtures/comms-workplace/prepare.sh /absolute/new/config
```

The destination must be new and its parent must already exist. Preparation delegates to the home/runtime source preparer, then copies this manifest, the shared Comms body and six COMMS.typify files. It does not copy PLAN, BUILD, old receipts, values, keys or runtime support, and it calls no reader or frame.

The source scopes are workplace, Harbor, Dock, Pilot, Watch and Keeper. Targets exercise all four scopes. Distinct actions use distinct selectors, so a fold that forgets the action cannot pass merely by reproducing one common permission matrix. The examples exercise a narrower asking scope against a globally narrower target and a narrower target within one asking scope.

Watch and Grower both have clearance 1 in the inherited source: Watch takes Harbor's value and Grower has a seat value. Watch can reach Grower by an explicit allowance in every action: the Harbor mail/write allowances and the seat-level grab allowance. No clearance row changes in this overlay. All grab/write allowances come from reach terms.

The mailbox position is `mailbox` under the eventual isolated workplace root. The support directory root/mailbox is deliberately outside the source-only preparation and must later be copied into that root, never into the separate configuration clone. It contains no real mailbox or request. Existing home/runtime support must likewise be supplied before a build, without treating empty placeholders as working tools.

Native formation, recorded events, the 75 mail/grab/write decisions, duplicate/conflict variants and symbolic request cases are separate private predictions, written before their measurements. The frame supplies policy decisions and the carrier; declarations prove neither permission enforcement nor delivery.
